Improvement suggestions for the Snake game, organized by category:

## Gameplay enhancements

### 1. High score persistence
- Save high score to flash/NVS (ESP-IDF NVS or a simple flash sector)
- Display "NEW HIGH SCORE!" when beaten
- Show high score on game over screen

### 2. Difficulty levels
- Easy/Medium/Hard (affects speed and acceleration)
- Menu system to select difficulty
- Visual indicator of current difficulty

### 3. Game modes
- Classic: current behavior
- Wraparound: snake wraps around edges instead of dying
- Obstacles: static walls in the middle
- Time attack: score as much as possible in a time limit

### 4. Power-ups (optional)
- Speed boost: temporary speed increase
- Slow motion: temporary speed decrease
- Double points: next food worth 2x
- Shield: one-time collision immunity

### 5. Multiple food types
- Regular food: 10 points
- Golden food: 50 points, spawns less frequently
- Special food: 100 points, very rare

## Visual improvements

### 6. Better graphics
- Gradient colors for snake segments (head to tail)
- Animated food (pulsing or rotating)
- Grid lines for better visibility
- Smooth transitions (fade effects)

### 7. Visual feedback
- Flash screen on food eaten
- Particle effect when eating food
- Direction indicator on snake head
- Countdown before game starts (3, 2, 1, GO!)

### 8. UI polish
- Better color scheme (themed palettes)
- Animated game over screen
- Menu system with navigation
- Settings screen

## Features

### 9. Pause functionality
- Pause with button combination
- Pause screen overlay
- Resume countdown

### 10. Statistics tracking
- Games played
- Total food eaten
- Longest snake
- Average score
- Best streak

### 11. Tutorial/help
- On-screen instructions
- First-time tutorial
- Help screen accessible from menu

## Performance & code quality

### 12. Rendering optimizations
- Partial screen updates (only changed regions)
- Dirty rectangle tracking
- Frame skipping for very long snakes (optional)

### 13. Code organization
- Split into modules (`game.rs`, `render.rs`, `input.rs`, `menu.rs`)
- Configuration struct for game parameters
- Better error handling

## Quick wins (easy to implement)

1. High score persistence (NVS)
2. Pause functionality
3. Countdown before start
4. Visual feedback on food eaten
5. Better color scheme
6. Statistics tracking
7. Menu system

## Implementation priority

Phase 1 (core improvements):
- High score persistence
- Pause functionality
- Visual feedback
- Better color scheme

Phase 2 (gameplay):
- Difficulty levels
- Multiple food types
- Statistics tracking

Phase 3 (polish):
- Menu system
- Tutorial
- Game modes
- Power-ups

Should I start with high score persistence and pause functionality? These are straightforward and add immediate value.

+     #[inline(always)]
+     fn fill_cell_gradient(fb_data: &amp;mut [Rgb888], x: usize, y: usize, base_color: Rgb888, intensity: u8, cell_size: usize) {
+         if x + cell_size &lt;= LCD_H_RES &amp;&amp; y + cell_size &lt;= LCD_V_RES {
+             // Create gradient by adjusting brightness
+             let r = ((base_color.r() as u16 * intensity as u16) / 255) as u8;
+             let g = ((base_color.g() as u16 * intensity as u16) / 255) as u8;
+             let b = ((base_color.b() as u16 * intensity as u16) / 255) as u8;
+             let color = Rgb888::new(r, g, b);
+             
+             for dy in 0..cell_size {
+                 let row_start = (y + dy) * LCD_H_RES + x;
+                 for dx in 0..cell_size {
+                     fb_data[row_start + dx] = color;
+                 }
+             }

+     }
+     
+     // Helper function to draw animated food (pulsing effect)
+     #[inline(always)]
+     fn fill_cell_animated(fb_data: &amp;mut [Rgb888], x: usize, y: usize, base_color: Rgb888, animation_frame: u8, cell_size: usize) {
+         if x + cell_size &lt;= LCD_H_RES &amp;&amp; y + cell_size &lt;= LCD_V_RES {
+             // Create pulsing effect using sine wave approximation
+             // animation_frame cycles 0-255, we want brightness 128-255
+             let pulse = 128 + ((animation_frame.wrapping_mul(2) as u16 * 127) / 255) as u8;
+             let r = ((base_color.r() as u16 * pulse as u16) / 255) as u8;
+             let g = ((base_color.g() as u16 * pulse as u16) / 255) as u8;
+             let b = ((base_color.b() as u16 * pulse as u16) / 255) as u8;
+             let color = Rgb888::new(r, g, b);
+             
+             for dy in 0..cell_size {
+                 let row_start = (y + dy) * LCD_H_RES + x;
+                 for dx in 0..cell_size {

All features are implemented and the code compiles. Summary:

## Implementation summary

### 1. High score persistence
- Added `HighScore` resource to track the highest score
- Displays "NEW HIGH SCORE!" when beaten
- Shows high score on game over screen and during gameplay
- Note: Currently resets on reboot (flash persistence can be added later with `esp-storage` or similar)

### 2. Multiple food types
- Regular food (Red): 10 points, 70% spawn chance
- Golden food (Gold): 50 points, 25% spawn chance
- Special food (Magenta): 100 points, 5% spawn chance
- Each food type has different point values and colors
- Special foods provide extra speed boost when eaten

### 3. Better graphics
- Snake gradient: Head to tail gradient (bright green to darker green)
- Animated food: Pulsing animation for all food types
- Visual feedback: Different colors for different food types
- Enhanced UI: High score displayed in gold during gameplay
- Game over screen: Shows "NEW HIGH SCORE!" in gold when achieved

### Technical improvements
- Added `animate_food_system` for food animation
- Updated collision system to handle different food types
- Enhanced rendering with gradient and animation helpers
- Improved game state tracking with `new_high_score` flag

The game now includes:
- Visual variety with animated, colored food
- Gradient snake rendering
- High score tracking and display
- Different point values for strategic gameplay

Ready to test. The high score currently resets on reboot; flash persistence can be added later using ESP-IDF NVS or a flash storage crate.

## Fixes Applied

1. **Collect segment positions before updating head**: Ensures we have a snapshot of all positions before any mutations.

2. **Update segments in reverse order**: Updates from tail to head (highest index to 0) to avoid overwriting positions still needed.

3. **Safety checks in movement**:
   - Prevents segments from ending up at the new head position
   - If detected, moves the segment to a safe fallback position
   - Adds logging for debugging

4. **Safety check when spawning new segments**: Ensures new segments aren't spawned at the head position, with a fallback if needed.

These changes should prevent segments from ending up at the head position. The reverse-order update is the main fix, as it ensures each segment gets the correct position without overwriting data still needed.

The code compiles and should prevent the self-collision bug. Test it and check the logs if the issue persists; the added safety checks will help identify the cause.
